The BCA Method

NOT RANDOM FITNESS.
A DEVELOPMENT PROCESS.

Every BCA athlete goes through the same five-step process. We find out how your child moves, build the right qualities for their age and sport, and test regularly so you can see exactly what’s improving.

01

ASSESS

Understand how an athlete moves, accelerates, changes direction, jumps and controls their body.

02

DEVELOP

Build age-appropriate physical qualities around the athlete's stage, sport and individual needs.

03

TRAIN

Structured sessions built around speed, strength, power, coordination, movement and resilience.

04

MEASURE

Use repeatable testing to see what is improving and where the next opportunity lies.

05

PROGRESS

The programme evolves as the athlete grows, so development stays purposeful rather than repetitive.

How BCA Tests

WE MEASURE IT.
THEN WE IMPROVE IT.

Every BCA block starts and ends with the same seven tests, so you see real numbers — not opinions. The results set your athlete’s priorities for the next six weeks, and the retest shows exactly what changed.

0110m SprintAcceleration

The first three steps. Winning the race to a loose ball, reaching a drop shot, getting away from a defender.

Best of 3 from a standing start, timed.
02505 Turn — L & RChange of Direction

How fast they stop and turn — and whether one side is weaker than the other.

Run in, turn on a line, sprint 5m out. Tested off each foot.
03T-DrillAgility

Moving well in every direction, not just straight lines.

Forward, sideways both ways, backwards — one timed run.
04Standing Broad JumpPower

The leg power behind every sprint start, jump and push-off.

Two-footed jump for distance. Must stick the landing.
05Hop & Stick + Line HopsControl

Landing, cutting and stopping safely — a big part of staying injury-free — plus quick, coordinated feet.

Hop and freeze on each leg, scored 0–3. Then side-to-side line hops for 15 secs.
06Plank HoldCore

A strong trunk for changing direction, shielding, hitting and throwing.

Straight line head to heels. Max 60–180 secs by age.
07Sport Skill TestSport Speed

Speed that shows up in their actual sport, not just on a test.

Matched to their sport — e.g. slalom dribble for football, shuttle with a racket for tennis.
Week 1 · BaselineWeek 6 · Retest & reportEvery block · New prioritiesUnder-10s · Fun, game-style versions

The Science

WHY STEADY STATE CARDIO
ISN’T ENOUGH.

2M+
People Studied
A comprehensive analysis of over 2 million people found that muscle power is a stronger predictor of longevity than strength alone. Not endurance. Not flexibility. Power.
40s
When It Starts
Fast-twitch muscle fibre decline accelerates after your fourth decade. These are the fibres responsible for explosive movement, power output and fall prevention. They don’t respond to jogging.
Type II
The Fibres That Matter
Fast-twitch Type II fibres are your safety net — helping you move quickly, absorb impact and stay injury-free. Research confirms that sprint and power training preserves them. Endurance training alone does not.
Use It
Or Lose It
Long, low-intensity endurance work may actually reduce fast-twitch capability over time. The adults who move like athletes into their 50s and 60s are the ones who never stopped training explosively.
Who This Is For
🏃
Former Athletes

🎾

⚡

🛡️
Injury Prevention Focus
You've had injuries and want to move better, absorb impact more efficiently and build the resilience to stay active for decades.
What We Build
1
Sprint Mechanics
How to actually run fast. Posture, arm drive, acceleration phase, stride efficiency. Most adults have never been taught this — and it changes everything.
2
Explosive Power
Broad jump, bounding, plyometrics. The fast-twitch stimulus your body needs to preserve power output and protect against age-related decline.
3
Agility & Reaction
Change of direction speed, reactive movement, lateral quickness. The movement quality that keeps you sharp in sport and in daily life.
4
Movement Quality
Mobility, stability and correct mechanics under load. Building a body that moves efficiently, absorbs impact well and stays injury free.
5
Benchmarking & Progression
Sprint times, agility scores, power outputs — measured, tracked and improved. You'll know exactly what's getting better and why.

THIS ONLY WORKS IF YOU'RE ALL IN

24 in-person sessions over 3 months is a real commitment — from your child, and from you. This isn't a video library to dip into when it suits. It's twice-weekly, face-to-face coaching, backed by nutrition guidance, built for families who want a genuine result at the end of it, not just a programme they started.

Speed

Get faster, provably

Fast-twitch focused training from session one — the type of work that actually changes how quickly an athlete moves, not just how tired they get. Every programme starts with a real baseline and ends with the same tests again. You don't have to take our word for whether it worked. The numbers tell you.

Athleticism

Move well in every direction

Straight-line speed is one skill. Changing direction, decelerating under control, reacting to what's actually happening — that's what separates an athlete who looks fast from one who competes fast. Three months of hands-on coaching is enough time to build both properly.

Armour

Built to last, not just to perform

Most speed programmes skip this part. Ours doesn't. Deceleration training, shoulder and rotator cuff health, trunk stability — the unglamorous work that keeps a young athlete on the pitch or the court instead of on the sidelines.

THREE MONTHS, THREE PHASES

Strength first, then speed, then stability under fatigue — the order that actually holds up, coached in person every step.

MONTH 1 — FOUNDATION & STRENGTH
Build the platform everything else stands on

Baseline testing in session one, then in-person sessions building real strength — unilateral work, core stability, controlled movement patterns. This is the least glamorous month and the most important one.

MONTH 2 — SPEED & POWER
Turn that strength into fast-twitch speed

Sprint mechanics, reactive agility, explosive power work — now that the foundation is there, coaching shifts toward pure speed and first-step quickness.

MONTH 3 — STABILITY & ARMOUR
Make it hold up under real match conditions

Deceleration, direction change under fatigue, and the injury-resilience work most programmes never get to. Finishes with a full retest against the Month 1 baseline.

NUTRITION, BUILT IN

Training doesn't work in isolation. Alongside the in-person sessions, your BCA coach works directly with the athlete and family on fuelling properly for training and recovery — simple, practical guidance that fits real family life, not a restrictive diet plan.

This is general nutrition guidance as part of coaching, not clinical or medical dietary advice. Any specific dietary needs, conditions, or concerns should go through a GP or a qualified sports nutritionist.

Why This Isn't Just A Video Library

DISTANCE ISN'T THE PROBLEM. GENERIC PROGRAMMES ARE.

Most online training is the same plan sent to everyone. BCA Online Performance starts with a real questionnaire and BCA Screening, so your programme is built around your actual sport, goals and current level — then adjusted as your BCA coach reviews your progress, not left on autopilot for three months.

HOW IT WORKS

The same BCA Athlete System used in every in-person programme — two 6-week blocks, back to back, building your 3-month picture.

STEP 1
Athlete & Parent Onboarding

Training background, current goals, sport, availability and any injury history — the full picture before anything is programmed.

STEP 2
Initial Assessment

Movement (squat, lunge, single-leg control, hinge, landing mechanics), speed (10m & 20m), change of direction, power (broad jump, vertical, reactive jump) and strength — scored across 8 athletic qualities to build your Top 3 Priorities.

STEP 3
Block 1 — 6 Weeks

Baseline, Load, Power, Peak, Endurance, Retest — built around your Top 3 Priorities, not a generic template. Sprinters and track athletes get a dedicated speed-focused emphasis throughout.

STEP 4
Progress Report & Block 2

Week 6 retest compared against your baseline, a written report from your BCA coach, then a second 6-week block building on exactly what the numbers showed.

STEP 5
Weekly Structure & Video Guides

Clear weekly sessions with video demonstrations every week of both blocks, so technique is never a guess.

STEP 6
Final Retest & 3-Month Report

The same tests from Week 1, repeated at Week 12. A real comparison across the full 3 months, not a feeling.

INSIDE THE ATHLETE PORTAL.

Every programme is a 6-week block: a baseline test, progressive sessions with demo videos, a Week 6 retest and a report card. Your BCA coach matches you to the right programme and sport focus from your assessment. See a sample report →

About BCA
BCA is a coach-led athletic development company for young athletes, based in Cobham, Surrey. It follows one method for every athlete: Assess, Develop, Train, Measure, Progress. Each athlete has a BCA Screening, a personal programme approved by a BCA coach, coached sessions in person or online, sessions at home in the BCA app, and a retest every 6 weeks. BCA describes itself as your complete athletic partner.
Ben Cullen is the founder of BCA and a speed and agility specialist with 18 years of international coaching experience and 30 years in sport. He is a Senior Performance Coach at Ewell Castle Tennis Academy and the Surrey U18s Boys Head Coach. He works with the BCA coaching team, including strength and conditioning coach Cherrise Cleary Dowling.
The BCA app is where families and athletes follow their programme. After a short athlete profile, it builds a starting programme that a BCA coach confirms. It then gives today's session with a video for every drill, a week planner that works around training and matches, growth tracking, BCA Screening results, progress against the age group, messages with the coach and notifications. Under-13s get Kid mode with missions, stars and badges. BCA Scan measures movement technique and first-step reaction with the phone's camera, and the video never leaves the phone.
A BCA Screening is BCA's athletic assessment: speed (10 m sprint), change of direction (5-0-5), power (broad jump), landing and balance (hop and stick, left and right), agility (lateral hops), core (plank) and coach-scored movement quality, plus growth and maturity. It shows each athlete's strengths, focus areas and left-right differences, and it is repeated every 6 weeks to measure progress.
Yes. BCA runs athletic development programmes and testing days for schools, academies and clubs, including Ewell Castle Tennis Academy and Cobham Rugby Club. A squad is screened in about an hour, every athlete gets their own programme in the BCA app, and the coach sees the whole group's results. Programmes run in 6- or 12-week blocks, in person or online.
In person in Cobham and across Elmbridge and Surrey, including Esher, Oxshott, Weybridge, Walton-on-Thames and Ewell, at schools, clubs and BCA's own sessions. Online coaching through BCA Online Performance is available worldwide.
Yes. Tennis is one of BCA's core sports. Ben Cullen coaches at the UK's top-ranked tennis academy, and BCA programmes for tennis players focus on first-step speed, split-step reactions, lateral movement, braking and change of direction, plus injury resilience through growth spurts. BCA also coaches football, rugby, cricket, hockey, netball, athletics, dance and more.
Yes. Juniors aged 6-18 are BCA's core, and older athletes on the pathway into university, US college or professional sport are coached 1:1 or through BCA Online Performance. BCA partners with Sport USA for athletes going to US colleges on sports scholarships.
General
Ages 6–18 across the junior programmes, plus a dedicated programme for adults. Every programme is adapted to age, experience and readiness — testing is never one-size-fits-all.
Athletic foundations transfer to every sport — tennis, football, rugby, cricket, hockey, basketball and more. Personal coaching packages are fully tailored to your child's specific sport.
Very little. Most sessions need cones and a flat space — garden, park or court. Some use an agility ladder (under £10 on Amazon). No gym equipment needed.
Both. In-person in Cobham and Surrey. Online coaching available worldwide via BCA Online Performance and the members portal.
Programmes & Pricing
2 sessions per week for all online programmes. In-person frequency depends on the package — Intro Sessions is a one-off 2-session introduction, Athletic Fundamentals runs weekly on a monthly membership, and The BCA Blueprint runs at roughly 2 sessions per week across the full 3 months.
Yes. Memberships are monthly and you can cancel with one month’s notice. Intro Sessions, single sessions, BCA Online Performance and The BCA Blueprint are one-off payments, so there’s nothing to cancel.
Athletic Fundamentals is ongoing weekly coaching on a monthly membership (Squad or 1:1), or pay as you go. The Blueprint is a complete 3-month system: BCA Screening, 24 structured in-person sessions across three phases, nutrition guidance, and a full retest — for families who want the whole journey mapped out from day one.
The BCA Blueprint
Real physical change takes time. The Blueprint runs as two 6-week blocks back to back — the same system used in every BCA programme — so strength, speed and stability each get a proper phase, not a rushed introduction.
No. It's general, practical guidance on fuelling for training and recovery, delivered by your BCA coach as part of coaching. Any specific dietary needs, conditions or concerns should go through a GP or a qualified sports nutritionist.
Yes — the Blueprint is fully in-person, currently available in Cobham and Surrey. For athletes further away, BCA Online Performance runs the same assessment-and-retest system remotely.
BCA Online Performance
Yes. BCA Online Performance is built for exactly this — athletes anywhere in the world get the same assessment, programming and coaching relationship as an in-person athlete, just delivered remotely.
If you're local enough to see a BCA coach occasionally, Online Performance works well alongside an Athletic Fundamentals membership. If you want the full hands-on experience, The BCA Blueprint is the natural next step up.
Adults
Yes — it's built around adults regaining fast-twitch power, speed and injury resilience that fade with age and steady-state cardio alone. Same coaching quality, different focus and testing.
Sport USA
Sport USA handles the US college recruitment pathway — academic and sporting profiles, coach introductions, applications and scholarship negotiation. BCA builds the athletic side underneath it — the speed, strength and resilience that gets an athlete noticed by college coaches in the first place, and holds up once they're competing at that level.
Safety & Data
Yes. Personal and medical information is stored securely and only shared with third parties where necessary for your child's safety — for example, emergency services. Under UK GDPR you can request access to, correction of, or deletion of this data at any time.
Let your BCA coach know before the first session so training can be adapted appropriately. Physical training carries an inherent risk of injury even when planned and supervised carefully — this is explained fully as part of the onboarding consent process.

Free Athletic Starter Pack

THE BCA 7-DAY
ATHLETIC STARTER PACK

A practical introduction to speed, strength, movement and athletic confidence for young athletes aged 8–18.

Assess • Develop • Train • Measure • Progress

WELCOME TO BCA

This starter pack is designed to help young athletes begin developing the physical qualities that support performance in their sport.

You do not need a gym or expensive equipment. Most sessions can be completed in a small outdoor space with a few cones or household markers.

Important: this is general educational guidance, not a medical assessment or individualised training prescription. Young athletes should work within their ability, stop if they experience pain or dizziness, and have appropriate adult supervision.

THE BCA PERFORMANCE PILLARS

SPEED
How quickly you can move
ACCELERATION
How quickly you get started
MOVEMENT
How well you control your body
STRENGTH
How effectively you produce force
AGILITY
How well you change direction
REACTION
How quickly you respond
CONFIDENCE
How positively you attack challenges
RESILIENCE
How well you repeat quality efforts

HOW TO USE THE PACK

  • ▸Complete one session per day, or spread the seven sessions across two weeks.
  • ▸Warm up before every session.
  • ▸Focus on quality movement rather than rushing.
  • ▸Record how the session felt and note one thing you improved.
  • ▸Retest the final session and compare how you feel with Day 1.
The Programme

SEVEN DAYS. SEVEN SESSIONS.

Scroll through at your own pace — or jump to a day.

DAY 1
MOVEMENT & COORDINATION
Build body control, rhythm and confidence.
Warm-up
2 minutes of jogging, skipping or marching, followed by 10 arm circles and 10 bodyweight squats.
Main work
3 rounds: 20 seconds of fast feet; 20 seconds of lateral steps; 20 seconds of marching knee drives; 30 seconds rest.
Challenge
Move through a simple cone pattern forwards, sideways and backwards for 4 rounds.
Reflection
Which direction felt easiest? Which direction needs more control?
Day 1 done? Keep going

UNLOCK DAYS 2–7 — FREE

Message the BCA team on WhatsApp with your athlete’s age and sport and we’ll personally send you the unlock code for the rest of the pack — plus a tip on what to focus on for their sport.

Day 2 · AccelerationDay 3 · BalanceDay 4 · Change of DirectionDay 5 · StrengthDay 6 · ReactionDay 7 · Retest
Already have your code?
We’ll only use your details to send your code and reply to you — privacy policy.
That code doesn’t look right — check the message from BCA and try again.
DAY 2
ACCELERATION
Learn to start efficiently and project forward.
Warm-up
3 progressive runs at 50%, 65% and 75% effort.
Main work
6 × 10-metre accelerations. Start relaxed, lean slightly forward and build speed over the first few steps. Walk back to recover.
Technique focus
Push the ground away, keep the first steps powerful and avoid standing upright too early.
Reflection
Did you feel powerful from the first step or only after building speed?
DAY 3
BALANCE & STABILITY
Develop control through single-leg positions.
Warm-up
20 seconds each: balance on left leg, right leg, heel raises and controlled lunges.
Main work
3 rounds: 8 single-leg reaches each side; 8 reverse lunges; 20-second side plank each side; 10 calf raises.
Technique focus
Keep the knee aligned with the foot and control every repetition.
Reflection
Which side felt stronger or more stable?
DAY 4
CHANGE OF DIRECTION
Learn to slow down, plant and push away.
Warm-up
Side shuffles, low skips and 3 gentle decelerations.
Main work
Set two markers 3–5 metres apart. Sprint to one, slow down under control, plant and accelerate back. Complete 6–8 repetitions.
Technique focus
Lower your centre of mass, take shorter steps into the change and push out aggressively.
Reflection
Could you stay balanced while changing direction at speed?
DAY 5
STRENGTH FOUNDATIONS
Build basic force production with control.
Warm-up
10 squats, 10 glute bridges, 10 wall push-ups and 20 seconds of marching.
Main work
3 rounds: 10 squats; 8 reverse lunges each side; 8–12 press-ups or elevated press-ups; 12 glute bridges; 20-second plank.
Technique focus
Move through a comfortable range and maintain good posture.
Reflection
Which exercise challenged you most?
DAY 6
REACTION & COMPETITIVE SPEED
Respond quickly and make movement decisions.
Warm-up
2 minutes of light movement, then 5 quick direction changes.
Main work
Use a partner to call left, right, forward or back. React and move 3–5 metres. Complete 8–10 reactions with full recovery.
Solo option
Use numbered or coloured markers and react to a random number or colour generated by a parent.
Reflection
Did you react first with your eyes, feet or body?
DAY 7
RETEST & REFLECT
Repeat key qualities and identify progress.
Retest 1
Complete 3 × 10-metre accelerations and compare how the first steps feel with Day 2.
Retest 2
Complete 4 controlled changes of direction and focus on balance and push-off.
Retest 3
Repeat one strength circuit from Day 5 with excellent technique.
Reflection
Write down: one improvement, one ongoing challenge and one quality you want to develop next.
FINISHED THE 7 DAYS?

Tell us how it went and a BCA coach will personally let you know what your athlete should focus on next.

WHAT NEXT?

The starter pack is an introduction — not a complete long-term development plan. The next step is understanding the athlete as an individual: their sport, age, movement qualities, strengths, challenges and goals.

About Sport USA

15+ YEARS. $150M+ SECURED.

Sport USA helps talented student-athletes explore opportunities to combine higher education with competitive sport at universities across the United States. With over 15 years’ experience and more than $150 million secured in scholarships, Sport USA specialises in guiding athletes through the US college recruitment process, including NCAA, NAIA and JUCO programmes.

Their team includes former US college student-athletes who have experienced the pathway first-hand. They support students with assessing their academic and sporting potential, creating their athlete profile and highlight materials, connecting with suitable US college coaches, navigating eligibility and applications, and evaluating scholarship opportunities.

Sports Covered
Tennis, football, hockey, golf, rowing, swimming, athletics, basketball, rugby, lacrosse, volleyball and more

Their aim is to help young athletes understand the opportunities available within the US university system and identify a pathway that fits both their academic ambitions and sporting ability.

PRIVACY POLICY.

Last updated: 9 November 2026

This policy explains how Ben Cullen Athletics (“BCA”, “we”, “us”) collects and uses personal information about the athletes we coach and their parents or guardians. BCA is Ben Cullen Athletics Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales (company number 17567878), which is the data controller for the information described here.

Contact: ben@bencullenathletics.co.uk · 07818 260920

What we collect

  • Contact details – the parent or guardian’s name, phone number and email address (or the athlete’s own, for adult clients).
  • Athlete details – name, age, sport, training history, goals and availability.
  • Health information you choose to share – injuries, medical conditions or anything else we need to know to coach safely.
  • Training and progress records – assessments, test scores, session notes and programme progress.
  • Payment records – invoices and payments received. Payments are made by bank transfer; we don’t take or store card details.
  • Messages – anything you send us by WhatsApp, email, Instagram or through the website quiz and forms.

How we use it

  • To reply to enquiries, recommend a programme, and arrange and deliver coaching.
  • To plan training safely, track progress and share results with you.
  • To take payments and keep business and tax records.
  • To contact you about your sessions and, occasionally, relevant BCA programmes – you can ask us to stop at any time.

Our legal reasons for using it

  • Contract – to provide the coaching you have booked.
  • Legitimate interests – to answer enquiries, run and improve the business, and keep athletes safe.
  • Explicit consent – for health information, which you give when you share it. You can withdraw consent at any time, although we may then be unable to coach safely.
  • Legal obligation – to keep financial records and, where required, safeguarding records.

Children’s information

For athletes under 18, we collect information from, and communicate with, a parent or guardian. We only collect what we need to coach safely and well. Athletes aged 13 to 17 can have their own app login, but only if their parent or guardian invites them, and the parent can always see everything in that account, including messages.

Photos and video

We may film technique privately to give coaching feedback. We will never use photos or video of an athlete in marketing or on social media without the written consent of a parent or guardian (or the athlete, if over 18).

The BCA app

Members get a login to the BCA app (the athlete portal on this website). A parent or guardian holds the login for athletes under 18 and agrees to this policy before the dashboard opens. In the app we keep:

  • Account details – the parent’s email and name, and each athlete’s first name, sport, programme and age group.
  • Test results – speed, agility, jump and core tests and movement-quality scores entered by a BCA coach. Tests done on both sides are compared (left vs right) so we can add balance work where one side lags. On a squad testing day, a member of the school or club’s staff may help enter results using a BCA helper login: they see only first names and age groups for their own squad, can’t see anything else in the app, and their login is removed after the day. Age-group averages are only shown when at least 5 athletes are included, to help protect each child’s individual scores.
  • BCA Scan – when you film a movement, the video is analysed on your own phone and is never uploaded to us. If you choose to save the result, we keep only the score and measurements (for example a knee angle), not the video.
  • Growth & maturity – height, and optionally sitting height, weight and both parents’ heights, with birth month and whether the growth formula for boys or girls applies. We use this to estimate growth spurts and adjust training. Weight, parents’ heights and the predicted adult height are only visible to BCA coaches and are never shown on the family dashboard. These are coaching estimates, not a medical assessment.
  • My week – the activities you add (for example tennis squad, matches, PE: day, minutes and how hard) and optional daily check-ins (sleep, energy, soreness on a 1–3 scale). We use these to balance training load. One-off activities are removed after their week.
  • Squad codes – if your club or school gives you a BCA squad code, you create your own login with it. The club or school never passes your child’s details to us. We record which squad your child is in so their programme is covered, and the club or school only ever sees squad totals and averages, never your child’s name or individual results.
  • About your athlete – the answers you give when you add your child: first name, month and year of birth, sport, position or event, level, season, goals, other sports, any areas of pain and an optional note. Pain and anything about injuries or conditions is health information: you choose to share it, it is only seen by BCA coaches, and we use it to keep training safe (for example, a coach checks before any hard sprints or jumps). You can update or remove these answers at any time.
  • Safety details – emergency contacts, who may collect your child, medical conditions, medication, allergies, anything that helps your child feel comfortable, your GP surgery, and your choices about emergency treatment, coaching video and photos. Only you and BCA coaches can see these (never testing-day helpers), and we use them only to keep your child safe at sessions. You can update them at any time from the Account tab.
  • Messages – messages between your family and the BCA coaching team in the app, with who sent them and when. Parents can always read every message in their child’s thread, including ones their teen sends or receives. When a new message arrives we send a short email alert that only says a message is waiting; the message itself is never put in the email.
  • Teen logins – if a parent invites their 13–17-year-old, we keep the teen’s email address so they can sign in. Teens can see their own programme, results and week and message the coaches; they can’t change consent, growth details or data requests, which stay with the parent. The parent can remove the teen’s login at any time, which deletes it. Children under 13 don’t get their own login: they use Kid mode on the parent’s phone, which is locked with a PIN that is stored only on that phone.
  • Training plans – the BCA Engine suggests training priorities from the information above using clear coaching rules. As soon as you complete the athlete profile it builds a starting programme, clearly marked “awaiting BCA confirmation”. Until a BCA coach confirms it, sessions stay gentle (low-impact, level 1 only). A BCA coach reviews and confirms every programme; the engine never increases training on its own.
  • Missions and rewards – when a session is marked done we record the date, which gives the stars, badges and weekly streak in Kid mode. These are only shown to your family and your coach.
  • Notifications – if you turn on notifications, we keep the technical address your phone’s browser gives us for sending them (no name, email or location). Notifications never include message text, results or health details: only a short nudge such as “New message from your BCA coach”. Turn them off at any time in the Account tab or your phone settings, and we delete that address.
  • What you’re signing up for – when you add your child you tell us whether it’s app only, a group class, 1:1 coaching or the BCA Blueprint. App-only families aren’t asked for emergency contacts or collection details, because there are no in-person sessions.
  • Training background – optionally, how long your child has done any fitness training and roughly how many hours of sport they do each week, so the starting programme is pitched at the right level.
  • Live online sessions – if you and your BCA coach agree a video session instead of meeting in person, we keep the date, time, length, video link and any note. Sessions take place on the video service in the link (for example Zoom, Google Meet, Teams or WhatsApp) and are never recorded. For athletes under 18, a parent or guardian must be at home during the session.
  • Your BCA coach – we record which BCA coach looks after your child, and your family sees that coach’s first name.
  • Staying signed in – the app keeps you signed in on your device, like other apps, until you tap Log out. On a shared phone or tablet, please log out when you’ve finished.
  • Kid mode extras – the athlete your child designs, their Reaction Hero best score and their Move of the day ticks are saved on your own device only. They aren’t sent to us.
  • Drill videos – demo videos play inside the app using YouTube’s privacy-enhanced mode (youtube-nocookie.com). YouTube only receives the usual technical information when a video is played.
  • Usage – when you last opened the app and how many times, so we can support families who need help getting started.

Growth tracking and saving scan results are optional. You choose them on the consent screen and can change your mind at any time from Your data on the dashboard or by emailing us.

App data is stored securely with Amazon Web Services in London (UK), encrypted, with access limited to the BCA coaching team.

Who we share it with

We never sell your information. We only share it where needed with:

  • Service providers that help us run BCA, such as email, WhatsApp, website hosting and accounting tools.
  • Schools or clubs, where your child takes part in a programme delivered through that school or club. We share squad totals and averages only, never individual results, unless you ask us to.
  • Emergency services or medical professionals, if needed for an athlete’s safety.
  • Authorities, where the law or safeguarding duties require it.

Some of these providers may store data outside the UK. Where they do, they use recognised safeguards to protect it.

Our website

  • We don’t use advertising cookies on this site. If we add analytics or advertising tools in future, we’ll update this policy.
  • If you unlock the free starter pack, a small note is saved in your own browser so you don’t need to re-enter the code. It isn’t sent to us.
  • Demo videos are embedded from YouTube in privacy-enhanced mode. YouTube may set its own cookies when you play a video.

How long we keep it

  • Coaching and contact records, including app data: while the athlete trains with us, then for 2 years after the last session. After that we delete it, or keep only anonymous figures that can’t identify your child (for age-group averages).
  • Payment and business records: 6 years, as required for tax purposes.
  • Enquiries that don’t lead to coaching: up to 12 months.
  • Safeguarding or incident records: as long as required by law or safeguarding guidance.

Your rights

You can ask to see the information we hold, correct it, delete it, restrict or object to how we use it, or receive a copy to take elsewhere. Just email ben@bencullenathletics.co.uk. You can also use Your data at the bottom of your app dashboard. We’ll respond within one month.

If you’re unhappy with how we’ve handled your information, please tell us first. You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

Changes

We may update this policy from time to time. The latest version will always be on this page.

BOOKING TERMS.

Last updated: 9 November 2026

These terms apply to all coaching booked with Ben Cullen Athletics Ltd (“BCA”), a company registered in England and Wales (company number 17567878). By booking a session, block or programme, you agree to them. If anything is unclear, just ask before booking.

1. Bookings and payment

  • Single sessions and Intro Sessions are invoiced when you book and paid in advance by bank transfer, before the session.
  • Programmes such as the BCA Blueprint are paid as shown at the time of booking.
  • Prices are as listed on this website when you book.

2. Cancelling or moving a session

  • Give at least 24 hours’ notice and we’ll move your session to another time at no cost.
  • Sessions cancelled with less than 24 hours’ notice, or missed without notice, count as used.
  • If we have to cancel – for example because of weather, coach illness or venue issues – we’ll rearrange the session or credit it. You will never lose a session we cancel.

3. Memberships

  • Memberships are paid monthly in advance, on the 1st of each month, by standing order. Paying for a term in advance saves 5%.
  • You can cancel at any time with one month’s notice.
  • Membership sessions are for the month they’re paid for and can’t be carried over. If we cancel a session, we’ll always rearrange it.
  • We’ll let you know about holiday weeks in advance.

4. Your right to cancel

  • If you book online or by phone, message or email, you have 14 days from booking to cancel for a full refund.
  • If you ask for coaching to start within those 14 days and then cancel, we’ll refund you minus the sessions already delivered.
  • After 14 days, unused sessions are not normally refundable. If something serious happens, such as a long-term injury, speak to us and we’ll always try to find a fair solution.

5. Health and safety

  • Please tell us about any injuries, medical conditions or medication before the first session, and let us know if anything changes.
  • Athletes should wear suitable sports clothing and footwear and bring water.
  • Athletes should tell the coach straight away if they feel pain, dizziness or unwell. We’ll stop or adapt the session.
  • All physical training carries some risk of injury. We plan and supervise every session carefully to keep that risk as low as possible.

6. Supervision and safeguarding

  • A parent or guardian is responsible for athletes under 18 before and after their session. Please drop off and collect on time.
  • BCA coaches are enhanced DBS checked, safeguarding trained, first aid qualified and insured.
  • If you have any concern about an athlete’s welfare, please contact BCA’s safeguarding lead, Ben Cullen, directly.
  • Live online sessions: for athletes under 18, a parent or guardian must be at home for the whole session. Sessions use the link your BCA coach sends from the BCA app, are never recorded, and take place in a shared space at home (not a bedroom). Please make sure there’s enough clear space and a non-slip floor.

7. Photos and video

We may film technique to give private coaching feedback. We will never use photos or video of an athlete in marketing without written consent.

8. Online programmes, portal and starter pack

  • Online programmes, portal logins and unlock codes are for the booked athlete only. Please don’t share logins or content.
  • Online and free content is general guidance. Athletes should train within their ability, with adult supervision where appropriate.

9. Our responsibility to you

Nothing in these terms limits our liability for death or personal injury caused by our negligence, or anything else that cannot be limited by law. Otherwise, our liability is limited to the price you paid for the coaching concerned. These terms don’t affect your statutory rights.

10. General

We may update these terms from time to time; the version on this page when you book will apply. These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.

ATHLETIC DEVELOPMENT.
BUILT FOR SPORT.

Every young athlete has potential. We help develop it.

A coach-led athletic development pathway for young athletes aged 6–18, supported by the BCA app. Real coaches assess, plan and guide every athlete, and parents see the whole journey.

Register interest Schools & clubs
Speed & agility specialists18 years international coachingSurrey U18 Boys Head CoachWorking with Ewell Castle & Cobham Rugby juniors
The BCA Method

ONE PATHWAY. AGES 6 TO 18.

01
Assess

Movement scans, speed and agility tests, growth measurements, and the athlete’s sport and training week.

02
Develop

Priorities for their sport, suggested by the BCA Engine and reviewed, edited and approved by a BCA coach.

03
Train

A weekly programme with demo videos, plus in-person or online sessions with the BCA team.

04
Measure

A retest every 6 weeks: tests, scans and growth, compared with where they started.

05
Progress

A clear report for parents, new priorities, and training adjusted as they grow.

The BCA app

MORE THAN A TRAINING APP.

BCA connects the athlete, the parent and the coach. Technology supports the process. Coaches lead the development.

Real app screens, shown with a sample athlete.

  • ✓Movement Scan: squat, press-up, hinge, plank, lunge, jump & land, sprint start and change of direction
  • ✓Speed, agility and jump tests, retested every block
  • ✓Growth & maturity tracking (estimates, interpreted by a coach)
  • ✓Sport-specific priorities approved by a BCA coach
  • ✓Weekly programme with demo videos
  • ✓One parent login for every child in the family

Scan videos are analysed on the phone and never uploaded. A parent holds the account for every athlete under 18.

Built for sport. Built for every athlete.

A TENNIS PLAYER DOESN’T MOVE LIKE A FOOTBALLER.

BCA builds the athletic foundations underneath every sport, alongside your child’s sport coach, not instead of them.

Tennis

Split step, first step, lateral strength and braking.

Football

Acceleration, turning, deceleration and power.

Rugby

Strength, power, acceleration and landing control.

Every athlete

Coordination, balance, strength and confidence, whatever their sport.

For families
A CLEAR PATHWAY FOR YOUR CHILD.

See their progress, follow a structured programme, and have a BCA coach who knows them. Sporty or not.

Parent information packs, family and team programmes, in person or online, with testing and coach-approved plans. Start with a small pilot.

Our philosophy

NOT EVERY YOUNG PERSON DEVELOPS AT THE SAME RATE. NOT EVERY SPORT DEMANDS THE SAME QUALITIES. SO NOT EVERY ATHLETE NEEDS THE SAME PROGRAMME.

That’s why BCA puts the athlete first: structured, individual, and built around their sport and their stage of growth.
